diagnostic_evidence.quote: Our method attains comparable error with $N=120$ dof on a square torus with three trefoil-shaped holes.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper proves only well-posedness of the continuous integral equations (Theorems 1-3). It gives no error analysis of the Nyström/Kress-splitting discretization, so spectral convergence is only observed in a few examples, not shown. The 'faster than MPS' claim rests on one anecdotal comparison between different problems: about 500 dof for two trefoil holes in the cited work versus 120 dof for three trefoil holes here. The error levels are matched only loosely (about 3e-6 versus comparable), and the paper's own error at N=150 is 4e-8.

failure_location.quote: is shown to be spectrally convergent, and has a faster convergence rate than the method of particular solutions for problems on tori with irregularly shaped holes

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract and Section 4 to say the method is 'observed numerically' to converge spectrally in the tested examples. Either remove the claim of a faster rate than MPS or support it with a like-for-like comparison on identical geometries and error norms.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of spectral convergence and the comparative-rate claim over MPS are unsupported as stated. The well-posedness theorems themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Spectral convergence and superiority over MPS claimed as 'shown' without analysis or like-for-like comparison
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained rewording or an added experiment, but it withdraws a substantive advertised guarantee (a proved rate and superiority) rather than a typo.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation of Re f_D = D[φ] uses the complex line element dξ = ξ'(t)dt, which supplies the factor ν = -iξ'/|ξ'|. The definition (and the Cauchy-integral analogue) uses the real arc-length measure |dξ|, which drops that factor. With |dξ| the identity Re f_D[φ] = D[φ] is false. The proof of the lemma and the later periodicity computations silently revert to dξ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |dξ| by the complex differential dξ in the definition of f_D and in the Cauchy-integral display. Keep the other terms as they are, since the proof already uses dξ.
issues.overall_effect: As defined, Lemma 2.6(1)-(2) is not correct. The uses of f_D in Lemma 2.4(4) and Lemma 2.7 rest on the intended complex-differential version, so those arguments are valid only after the definition is corrected.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential defined with arc length |dξ| so that Re f_D ≠ D[φ]
issues.why_classification: The proof already works with the intended definition, so a local one-symbol correction preserves all claims.

issues.failure_explanation: Since z - z̄ = 2i Im z, we have (z - z̄)² = -4(Im z)². Hence (z - z̄)²/(8b) = -Im(z)²/(2b), not +Im(z)²/(2b). The claimed identity in the proof is false, so Re f_G = -(1/2π)log|ϑ_1| - Im(z)²/(2b) ≠ G as defined in (eqn: green).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term by -(z-\bar z)^2/(8b), or equivalently by Im(z)^2/(2b) written without the conjugate, and fix the verification line accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 2.6(3) is false as stated. Nothing else in the paper depends on it, and the correct function has the opposite sign on the quadratic term.
issues.title: Sign error in f_G: Re f_G equals G only with the opposite sign of the quadratic term
issues.why_classification: Only the sign of one term changes, and no other result uses it.

issues.failure_explanation: The continuous problem (e: steklov bie) has right-hand side σ S_0[φ] = σ(S(I-M)φ + Mφ). The discrete problem uses σ S(I-M)φ and drops the +Mφ term. The additive constant in u = S_0[φ] is exactly what the paper says must be exact (the boundary values of u must match). The matrix problem therefore does not discretize (e: steklov bie), and its eigenvalues differ in general. The reconstruction formula that follows does include φ̄, so it is inconsistent with the eigenproblem it is applied to.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the discrete operator σ(S(I-M) + M)φ on the right-hand side, consistent with S_0 and with the reconstruction formula for u.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the Steklov algorithm does not compute the eigenvalues characterized by Theorem 1.3. The reported accuracy of about 1e-14 cannot be attributed to the displayed formulation.
issues.title: Discrete Steklov eigenproblem omits the mean term of S_0 and is inconsistent with the stated boundary integral equation
issues.why_classification: The fix is to add one matrix term that is already defined (M), and the method and conclusions are unchanged.
